memoryText: And Jesus said to him, If you can! All things are possible for one who believes.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Mark 9:23 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Jesus says this to a father whose son is tormented. The father had said, “If you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.” Jesus takes his word and turns it back.

“If you can!” Jesus is almost surprised at the doubt in the question. It is not a question of whether Jesus can. The question is whether the father will trust. The “if” belongs not to Jesus’ power but to the father’s faith.

“All things are possible.” This is not a blank check to get whatever we want. It is a statement about the power of God available to those who trust him. All things that fit the will of God are possible, because he is God. The one who stills the storm and raises the dead is able.

“For one who believes.” The power is not in our believing but in the one we believe. Faith is the open hand that receives what God gives. Even a small and trembling faith can reach out to a great Savior.

Notice what the father does next. He says, “I believe; help my unbelief!” He does not pretend to a perfect faith. He brings his mixture of faith and doubt to Jesus. And Jesus heals his son.

When you feel your faith is too small, say this verse and then pray the father’s prayer. The weakest faith in the strongest Savior is enough.
weekInReview: This week you read the Psalm 89 vow to sing of the steadfast love of the LORD and his covenant with David. In Mark 7 and 8 you saw Jesus teach that it is the heart that defiles, heal a Gentile woman’s daughter, and ask the turning-point question, “Who do you say that I am?” Peter’s answer, “You are the Christ,” was followed by Jesus’ first teaching that the Christ must suffer. You went up the mountain and heard the Father say, “Listen to him.” You heard a father cry, “I believe; help my unbelief!” In Mark 10 you read the key verse: the Son of Man came to serve and give his life as a ransom for many. You met Bartimaeus, then watched the King enter Jerusalem, cleanse the temple, and silence every question. Finally, in the Olivet Discourse, he told you to stay awake.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said he came “to give his life as a ransom for many.” What does it mean that the price of your freedom was his life?
Peter confessed that Jesus is the Christ, and then resisted the idea of a suffering Messiah. Where do you want a Jesus without a cross?
The father prayed, “I believe; help my unbelief!” What belief and what unbelief do you bring to Jesus today?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for giving his life as a ransom for many.
Ask him to keep you awake to him.
